title: Plant Chromatin Immunoprecipitation
author: Laura Poza-Viejo
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.444gyyw
materials: Boil samples again at 98°C for 10 min with agitation in thermomixer to inactivate Proteinase K.

steps.title: Harvest Tissue
steps.instruction: Harvest 1-2 g of Arabidopsis or Brassica seedlings, leaf tissue, or inflorescence into a 50 ml conical centrifuge tube.

steps.title: Crosslink Tissue
steps.instruction: Crosslink the tissue using Phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) with 1% formaldehyde (FAA). For protein binding, perform dual crosslinking with 2 mM DSG (disuccinimidyl glutarate).

substeps.instruction: Place samples in a desiccator attached to a vacuum pump.
For Arabidopsis seedlings and inflorescences: crosslink for 5 + 5 min.
For Brassica leaves and inflorescences: crosslink for 5 min + 10 min + 10 min.

steps.title: Stop Crosslinking and Rinse
steps.instruction: Stop the crosslinking process and clean the tissue.

substeps.instruction: Add 2 M Glycine to a final concentration of 0.125 M (e.g., 2.5 ml of 2 M Glycine in 37 ml of water).
Vacuum for 5 min.
Remove tissue from vacuum and rinse twice with MilliQ water.
Remove excess water by placing seedlings on a paper towel.

steps.title: Freeze and Grind Tissue
steps.instruction: Freeze the crosslinked tissue in liquid nitrogen and store at -80°C. When ready, grind the tissue with a mortar in liquid nitrogen to a fine powder.

steps.title: Extract Chromatin
steps.instruction: Isolate the chromatin from the ground tissue through a series of washes.

substeps.instruction: Transfer powder to a 50 ml centrifuge tube and add 10 ml of Extraction Buffer 1; mix well to dissolve tissue.
Filter the solution through Miracloth into a 50 ml centrifuge tube; repeat until clear of big particles.
Centrifuge at 5000 xg for 10 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 1 ml of Extraction Buffer 2; transfer to a 1.5 ml centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 5000 xg for 10 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and resuspend pellet in 300 µl of Extraction Buffer 3.

steps.title: Purify Chromatin Pellet
steps.instruction: Further purify the chromatin pellet using a cushion method.

substeps.instruction: Add 600 µl of Extraction Buffer 3 to a clean eppendorf.
Carefully layer the 300 µl resuspended pellet solution on top of the 600 µl buffer.
Centrifuge at 16000 xg for 60 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant and resuspend the chromatin pellet in 200 µl of Nuclei Lysis Buffer 3 by pipetting up and down (keep cold).
Take a 5 µl aliquot of each sample to check sonication efficiency.

steps.title: Prepare Antibody-Coated Dynabeads
steps.instruction: Prepare the magnetic beads for the specific antibody used.

substeps.instruction: Select Protein A beads for rabbit antibodies or Protein G beads for mouse antibodies.
Wash 15 µl Dynabeads in 500 µl ChIP dilution buffer twice.
Add 1-5 µg of antibody and incubate in 50 µl ChIP Dilution Buffer, rotating at 4°C for 1 h.
Wash beads with 500 µl of ChIP dilution buffer, attach to magnet, and discard buffer.
Resuspend Dynabeads in 50 µl of ChIP Dilution Buffer and keep on ice.
Measure the chromatin solution (typically ~150 µl).
Set aside 10% of the volume (e.g., 15 µl) as INPUT and store at -20°C.
Dilute the remaining chromatin solution 10 times by adding 1.5 ml of ChIP Dilution Buffer (reducing SDS from 1% to 0.1%).
Add antibody-coated Dynabeads into 750 µl of the diluted chromatin solution in a DNA low binding microtube.
Incubate rotating at 4°C overnight.

steps.title: Wash Immune Complexes
steps.instruction: Wash the beads the following morning at 4°C for 5 min with gentle rotation, using a magnet between washes.

substeps.instruction: Perform 2 washes with Low Salt Wash Buffer.
Perform 1 optional wash with High Salt Wash Buffer.
Perform 1 optional wash with LiCl Wash Buffer.
Perform 2 washes with TE Buffer.

steps.title: Elute Immune Complexes
steps.instruction: Elute the bound DNA from the beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µl of fresh Elution Buffer to the pelleted beads.
Vortex briefly and incubate at 65°C for 15 min with gentle agitation.
Attach beads to magnet and transfer 40 µl of supernatant to a new tube.
Repeat elution and combine the two eluates (Final volume = 80 µl).

steps.title: Reverse Crosslinking
steps.instruction: Reverse the protein-DNA crosslinks for both eluates and INPUT samples.

substeps.instruction: Add 3.2 µl 5 M NaCl to each ChIP eluate and to the INPUTs.
Incubate overnight at 65°C.

steps.title: DNA Purification via SPRI Beads
steps.instruction: Purify the resulting DNA using SPRI beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 180 µl (2.2x volume) of SPRI beads to the samples.
Mix by pipetting up and down at least 10 times and incubate for 5 min at room temperature.
Place tubes in magnet for 5 min and discard supernatant.
Wash SPRI beads four times with 100 µl of 70% ethanol (incubate 30 sec each time without disturbing beads), discarding supernatant after each wash.
Remove tubes from magnet and air dry beads for 4 min at room temperature.
Elute DNA in 30 µl of Tris-HCl 10 mM pH 8; mix by pipetting 10 times and incubate for 2 min.
Place tube on magnet for 5 min and transfer the supernatant (~25 µl) to a new tube.

steps.title: Alternative DNA Recovery (Chelex Method)
steps.instruction: Alternatively, elute immune complexes and INPUTs using Chelex resin.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µl 10% Chelex 100 resin (10 g in 100 ml water) to samples.
Boil at 98°C for 10 min with agitation in a thermomixer.
Cool on ice and incubate with 2 µl Proteinase K (10 mg/ml) at 37°C for 20 min.
Cool on ice and centrifuge at 16000 xg for 5 min at 4°C.
Transfer ~160 µl of supernatant (avoiding Chelex particles) to a DNA low binding microtube; store at 4°C or -20°C.
For ChIP-seq: Use 1-10 µl of DNA (concentration determined by Qubit fluorometer).
For real-time quantitative PCR: Use ChIP DNA directly, but dilute INPUT DNA at least 1:10 in water. Typically, 1-2 µl of DNA is sufficient for amplification.
